title: Arrays: a whole day in one variable

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the log here, and try your methods from main.

tasks.title: Read the last crossing
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `Crossings.java`, write a method called `lastCrossing`. It takes an `int[]` of passengers, one per crossing, and gives back an `int`: the passengers of the last crossing. The array always has at least one crossing, and it can be of any length.

Check calls `lastCrossing` with logs of its own, of different lengths, and reads what it gives back.
nextSteps: Write the first line: the parameter's type is `int[]`.
Work out the position of the last item of an array of 3, then of 6.
Write that position using the array's `length`, so it works for any length.
Try it from `main`, then try a typed-in position and read what happens.
hints: Positions start at 0, so the last position is not the length.
An array of length 3 has positions 0, 1 and 2. `passengers.length` gives the length of any array.

tasks.title: Add up the day
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a method called `total`. It takes an `int[]` of passengers and gives back an `int`: all of them added up. A day with no crossings, an empty array, has a total of 0.

Check calls `total` with logs of its own, an empty one included, and reads what it gives back.
nextSteps: Make a running total before the loop, as in the loops issue.
Loop over every position of the array, from the first to the last.
Add the item at each position to the total, and give the total back after the loop.
Try it from `main` with today's log.
hints: The positions of an array run from 0 to one less than its `length`.
With `i <= passengers.length` the loop asks for one position too many, and the program stops with an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`.
The loop is `for (int i = 0; i < passengers.length; i++) { sum = sum + passengers[i]; }`, with `sum` made at 0 before it.

tasks.title: Find the busiest crossing
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a method called `busiest`. It takes an `int[]` of passengers, with at least one crossing, and gives back an `int`: the position of the crossing that carried the most. If two carried the same most, give back the earlier one.

Check calls `busiest` with logs of its own, one with two busiest crossings, and reads what it gives back.
nextSteps: Keep the position of the best crossing so far, starting with the first.
When a crossing carried more than the best so far, keep its position instead.
Give the position back after the loop, and try a log with a tie.
hints: The task asks for a position, not a number of passengers. The passengers at the best position are `passengers[best]`.
Only replace the best when a crossing carried more, not the same: then a tie keeps the earlier one.
Start with `int best = 0;`, loop `i` from 1, and inside write `if (passengers[i] > passengers[best]) { best = i; }`.

tasks.title: Make the departures
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, write a method called `departures`. It takes two `int`s, `firstHour` and `crossings`, and gives back a new `int[]` with one hour for each crossing: `firstHour`, the hour after, and so on. For 7 and 3 that is 7, 8 and 9.

Check calls `departures` with hours and crossings of its own, none included, and reads every item of the array it gives back.
nextSteps: Make a new array with one place for each crossing.
Put an hour in each place, built from `firstHour` and the position.
Give the array back, and print its first and last item from `main`.
hints: `new int[n]` makes an array of `n` places, each starting at 0. Its type, for the method's first line, is `int[]`.
Position 0 holds `firstHour`, position 1 the hour after. The position says how many hours later.
Inside the method: `int[] hours = new int[crossings];`, then a loop with `hours[i] = firstHour + i;`, then `return hours;`.
